review.title: A superseded task needs a terminal state that is true
review.acceptance: A superseded task has a TRUTHFUL terminal representation, so that a provenance-invalid original whose work shipped under a named successor is neither left BLOCKED forever nor mislabelled as work nobody did. THE GAP, measured rather than asserted. control/policies.json lists eight statuses and exactly two are terminal: DONE and CANCELED. BLOCKED transitions only to BACKLOG, READY or CANCELED. There is NO cancel command on the CLI -- the reachable verbs are validate, sync, status, dispatch, claim, start, gate, review, approve, request-changes, done, block, unblock, release and event -- so CANCELED is currently reachable only by hand-editing control/tasks.json, which is the move the operating contract forbids. And scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs states at its gate-recording guard that CANCELED means 'there is no work to evidence', which is FALSE for a superseded original: the work exists, was reviewed and shipped under the successor's id. THE CONTROL PLANE ALREADY KNOWS ABOUT SUPERSESSION AND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ACT ON IT. The comment at the supersession detector says a corrective re-run supersedes its predecessor and 'the predecessor is left BLOCKED deliberately -- its provenance record is preserved as audit history rather than repaired, on the rule PL-0703 established', and that BLOCKED can never reach DONE so requireAllDependenciesDone gates every dependent forever. It reports and never repairs, by design. This task does not change that: it adds a way to SAY the thing the detector already notices. REQUIRED: a terminal status that means superseded and says so -- the implementer chooses the spelling and justifies it -- carrying a REQUIRED reference to the successor task id, validated to exist and to be DONE. A status that permits a null successor is not acceptable: the whole content of the claim is which task carries the work now. REQUIRED: a control-plane command to reach it, because a terminal state reachable only by hand-editing the source of truth is worse than no terminal state. The transition must be refused when the named successor is not DONE, and the audit event must carry both ids. REQUIRED: a superseded task must NOT count as DONE in progress figures and must NOT satisfy requireAllDependenciesDone by pretending to be complete. Whether it should satisfy a dependency AT ALL is the design question and the implementer must answer it explicitly: a dependent of a superseded task is almost certainly meant to depend on the successor, and the existing detector already reports exactly that -- so the safe answer may be that supersession does NOT satisfy the dependency and the detector's advice to repoint stands. REQUIRED: the four current instances are the acceptance test, and their subsumption was audited in round 73 before this task was filed. PL-0205 superseded by PL-0207 (DONE), PL-0401 by PL-0405 (DONE), PL-0601 by PL-0603 (DONE), PL-0703 by PL-0706 (DONE). In every case the successor's acceptance was read in full against the original's and found to be a strict superset, not merely a DONE task with a similar name. NOT IN SCOPE: repairing the four originals' provenance, which the reviewer has ruled cannot be done in place; automatically repointing dependencies, which the existing comment refuses on the ground that a self-modifying graph is a larger failure than the one it fixes; and any change that lets a superseded task reach DONE.
review.notes: Filed 2026-09-22 from the round-73 subsumption audit gpt-architect ordered at b034460. The reviewer's instruction was explicit: verify subsumption mechanically, preserve the originals' audit history, use a legitimate terminal transition ONLY if one exists and accurately describes the relationship, and -- if the control plane has no truthful terminal representation -- LEAVE THE TASKS BLOCKED AND IMPROVE THE MECHANISM RATHER THAN FALSIFYING HISTORY. The audit found subsumption in all four cases and found no truthful terminal state, so all four stay BLOCKED and this task is the second half of that instruction. The decisive evidence is the control plane's own words: CANCELED is documented in scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs as meaning 'there is no work to evidence', and for these four the work exists and was reviewed. control/tasks.json is in reviewDependencies rather than allowedPaths deliberately: this task builds the mechanism and does not transition the four originals, which is a separate decision for the reviewer once a truthful state exists.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck at the repository root on 398445d, its own invocation, never combined with lint or build. turbo 21/21, exit 0. The surface is .mjs and .json and .md, so typecheck proves only that nothing downstream of control/policies.json broke; the load-bearing checks for this task are the unit gate below. Also run: npm run repo:validate -> passed, exit 0, which reads control/policies.json and the generated views.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on 398445d. (1) node scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs -> 70 scenarios, exit 0 (was 69; scenario 10t is new). (2) npx turbo run test --force across the monorepo -> 20/20 tasks, exit 0. (3) npm run repo:validate -> passed. (4) node scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs validate against the live board -> valid, 68 tasks, 9 agents, with only the three pre-existing WARNs. SCENARIO 10t ASSERTS THE FOUR WAYS THIS COULD HAVE SHIPPED AS AN AUDIT FICTION, on fixtures rather than live data because the live board has four candidates and none is transitioned, so a live-reading scenario would pass by being inert: the status cannot exist without naming a successor; an unfinished successor is refused by the command AND by validate as a hand-edit; SUPERSEDED does not satisfy a dependency (the existing repoint error still fires) and is excluded from both halves of the completion ratio; and the status is refused from an ACTIVE task with a message naming the three statuses it is reachable from. It also asserts the back-pointer is written by the command, that supersessionReason is persisted rather than only printed, and that the audit event records from=BLOCKED -- which would read SUPERSEDED -> SUPERSEDED if the status were captured after the transition. NON-VACUITY PROVEN BY MUTATION: reverting the completion denominator to the old expression [status !== CANCELED] makes scenario 10t fail on its assertion [Overall completion: 1/3 executable tasks], exit 1; restored and re-run green, 70 scenarios. SMOKE-TESTED AGAINST REAL DATA IN A THROWAWAY COPY of control/ and scripts/, never the live tree: supersede PL-0205 --by PL-0207 succeeded, validate stayed clean, PL-0207.supersedes was written, the completion denominator moved 68 -> 67 and the status summary gained a SUPERSEDED: 1 line. Refusals exercised there too: self-pointer, a successor that is REVIEW and not DONE, a successor already declaring a different supersedes, a missing --reason, and a hand-edited SUPERSEDED with the pointer deleted. THE LIVE BOARD IS UNCHANGED -- the four originals are NOT transitioned here, control/tasks.json is a reviewDependency on purpose, and that decision is left to the reviewer now that a truthful state exists. STATED LIMITATION: there is no npm run ai:supersede alias, because package.json is outside this task allowedPaths and widening a write surface for a convenience alias is the scope creep this control plane exists to prevent.

review.title: A repo guard that times out under load is a guard nobody can read
review.acceptance: packages/media-inspection/src/net-policy-boundary.test.ts:396, the test named “is not restated by any file outside this package”, stops being a test whose result depends on machine load and on what is on disk, WITHOUT weakening the property it asserts. THE DEFECT, DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN NAMED. Its failure mode is 'Error: Test timed out in 5000ms', not an assertion failure -- the assertion has never reported a false offender; the test simply does not finish. Its listSourceFiles recurses into every directory under packages/ and apps/ with NO exclusions and reads every .ts file it finds: 3,680 files totalling 24.3 MB on the tree measured, of which 3,337 are under node_modules and the rest include build output. The set of files the property is actually about is 327, reachable in 1-2 ms once node_modules, .next, .turbo, dist and coverage are skipped. It is the only test in this repository whose runtime is a function of installed dependencies and build artifacts rather than of source, which is why it presents as intermittent: every other repo-walking guard here -- packages/net-policy/src/module-boundary.test.ts, packages/contracts/src/module-boundary.test.ts, packages/provider-sdk/src/stremio/net-policy-boundary.test.ts and apps/web/src/app/watch/route-loading-boundaries.test.ts -- is scoped to its own SRC_DIR or APP_DIRECTORY. THE REPRODUCTION GRADIENT, measured on 2026-09-22 at e24d51f on a 2-core container: the test body alone, idle with a warm page cache, 109 ms; the whole file in an isolated vitest run, 687 ms; the file under turbo run test --force with a warm cache, 849-995 ms; the same under turbo run test --force immediately after dropping the page cache, 3,048 ms. The observed failure happened on a run started immediately after the e2e suite had rewritten apps/web/.next and apps/web/dist/desktop -- thousands of freshly written files, a cold cache, background flushing, and up to nine other workspace vitest processes competing for two cores -- which is where that gradient crosses the 5,000 ms default testTimeout. REQUIRED: the walk must not descend into node_modules, .next, .turbo, dist or coverage, and the exclusion list must be stated with its reason rather than left as a magic array. REQUIRED: the property must not be narrowed to buy the speed -- it must still see every source file under packages/ and apps/ outside this package, and the implementer must show that a planted offender is still caught. A RAISED testTimeout IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE FIX ON ITS OWN: it moves the ceiling without removing the dependence on disk state, and the next person to add a dependency moves the runtime again. SECOND DEFECT, FOUND WHILE DIAGNOSING AND IN SCOPE: build output ALREADY contains the string this test looks for. Seven files under apps/web/.next and apps/web/dist/desktop carry a reference-path fragment naming m3u8-parser.d.ts inside bundled chunks. They are .js today so the .ts filter misses them, which means the test is one bundler-output change away from naming a build artifact as an offender and failing for a reason that has nothing to do with any source file. The exclusion above fixes the correctness hazard and the performance one with the same edit, which is the argument for doing it that way rather than by raising a timeout.
review.notes: Filed 2026-09-22 by claude-test while executing PL-0504's and PL-0701's gates. THIS IS THE FINDING gpt-architect ORDERED PRESERVED AND EXPLICITLY ORDERED NOT TO BE CALLED A FLAKE, at the round-73 verdict: 'Do not label that failure a flake. Preserve the finding and investigate on its next occurrence as previously directed.' This is that next occurrence, and the investigation is in the acceptance. The first occurrence, during PL-0503's gates, could not name the failing test because the capture grep discarded it; that was reported at the time as a capture error, not as a flake. This occurrence was captured in full: src/net-policy-boundary.test.ts > the m3u8-parser shim is referenced from the file that imports it > is not restated by any file outside this package. The earlier working hypothesis -- 2 cores, turbo concurrency 10, and this package having no vitest.config.ts unlike packages/contracts -- was partly right and insufficient. Contention is a necessary condition, not the cause. The cause is that the test reads 24.3 MB it has no reason to read, so its runtime tracks page-cache state and build-artifact volume, and contention only decides which side of the 5 s ceiling that lands on. Three full-monorepo runs on the same tree after the failure were green (252/252 in this package), which is exactly why a load-dependent test must not be judged by re-running it. packages/media-inspection/vitest.config.ts is in allowedPaths because the implementer may conclude the package needs one; that is a decision for the implementer and this task does not require it. apps/web/src/app/api/v1/playback/build-target.test.ts is in reviewDependencies rather than allowedPaths: it resolves a REPO_ROOT and walks directories too, so it is worth checking for the same shape, but nothing observed implicates it and widening this task to it would be a guess.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck at the repository root, its own invocation, never combined with lint or build. turbo 21/21, 58.075s, exit 0. Covers @liberty/media-inspection, whose tsconfig includes the edited test file, and the two reviewDependencies' owners.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on 7423255 under the exact conditions that previously produced the failure, not under easier ones. (1) THE FILE: npx vitest run src/net-policy-boundary.test.ts in packages/media-inspection -> 23 tests (was 21; two added), exit 0. (2) THE PACKAGE: npx vitest run -> 11 files, 254 tests, exit 0. (3) THE WHOLE MONOREPO, CACHE-BUSTED AND CACHE-COLD: sync; drop_caches; npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 tasks successful, exit 0, with net-policy-boundary.test.ts at 187ms. That is the same shape as the run that timed out: turbo concurrency on 2 cores, no turbo cache, and a cold page cache. BEFORE AND AFTER, measured rather than asserted. The whole file under turbo --force with a cold page cache: 3,048ms before, 187ms after. The raw scan in isolation: 11,570ms cold unexcluded (well past the 5,000ms testTimeout that produced the observed failure) versus 15ms excluded. File count 3,680 -> 327; bytes read 24.3 MB -> 4.3 MB. The single test in isolation, cold page cache: 42ms. THE PROPERTY WAS NOT NARROWED TO BUY THAT, and two new assertions are the evidence rather than the claim. 'still sees the source it is supposed to see' requires the scan to contain a NAMED witness on the far side of the apps/ root -- apps/web/src/app/api/v1/playback/session/handler.ts -- and requires more than 200 files, because a count alone can be met by any 200 files while a named witness cannot. 'catches a planted offender, and skips one planted in an excluded directory' writes the reference directive into two files in a temp tree, one under src/ and one under node_modules/, and requires exactly the first to be reported. It is driven against a temp tree rather than the repository deliberately: planting under apps/web/src would drop a stray module into a workspace whose own suites walk their source while this one runs. A RAISED testTimeout WAS NOT USED and the acceptance refuses it: it would move the ceiling without removing the dependence on disk state. The second defect is fixed by the same edit -- .next and dist are no longer walked, so the seven build-output files that already carry the reference string can never be reported whatever extension they take.

recommended.acceptance: The deliverable is a package and information boundary, not a recommender: eligibility is resolved upstream so recommendation can never make content playable, candidate generation may see only the active profile's explicit watchlist, that profile's progress and completion state, catalog metadata and already-resolved eligibility, and it returns content ids plus generator reasons so the reason trail survives the layer most likely to lose it
